title: P treats a lone directive label as inert, so a stub or route through it moves net N into that netclass
verifier_method: Rebuilt from scratch on my own layout (pr57pt/verify-probe-labels/v01_directive.py and .out): R1 at (63.5,76.2), N on R9, a .kicad_pro defining class HV. Cases: netclass_flag HV on the 1x stub path (a), at the stub end (b), on a pinless crossing wire (c), NEW c2 = flag on the FAR end of a pinless dangling wire whose other end is the stub end, controls d (plain crossing) and e (flag on a wire with pins), and g (connect_pins, flag on the H-first leg). Ran P, M, B; judged with kicad-cli 9.0.8 node sets plus per-node net class.

title: P's kept auto-junction at a label T splits the net it joins in kicad-cli 9, although the label alone already joins it
verifier_method: pr57pt/verify-probe-labels/v02_junction_split.py (.out): stub end on the interior of an N-net wire (a; a_rev drawn the other way), of the target's own wire (b), and NEW on the target's own straight outward wire (c; c_rev drawn toward the pin; d where that wire was drawn by the repo's add_wires). KiCad-only controls per case: P's geometry without the junction, with it, and with the hit wire pre-split at E1. Also seen in v03_stack_pin_merge.out.

title: P's model attaches a label to the wire under it even when a pin end shares the anchor, so a stub ending there merges a separate net into N
verifier_method: pr57pt/verify-probe-labels/v03_stack_pin_merge.py (.out): WN from R5:1 to R6:1 through E1 (both draw directions), R4:2's pin end and label N stacked at E1, plus a FOO variant; KiCad truth before, P/M/B, and P's geometry without the junction.

title: False no-op: P reports the pin already on N when KiCad detaches that label from the pin's wire
verifier_method: pr57pt/verify-probe-labels/v04_stack_own_wire.py (.out): target's own wire W1 from R1:1 to R2:1; at interior point Q, label N stacked with R4:1's pin end (a), an NC flag (b), label M (c), FOO plus pin (d), N plus pin plus a 2-point polyline (e), and NEW (f) label N plus a netclass flag; KiCad truth before each call, then P/M/B.

title: P refuses a legitimate call when a foreign label is stacked with a foreign pin on the target's wire
verifier_method: v04d in pr57pt/verify-probe-labels/v04_stack_own_wire.out (label FOO plus R4:1's pin end on W1's interior), KiCad truth before, P/M/B; v03b in v03_stack_pin_merge.out as a related stub-end case.

title: P as built has no 1 IU label capture: new stubs and labels within 1 IU of foreign labels or wires merge nets (off-grid only)
verifier_method: pr57pt/verify-probe-labels/v05_capture.py (.out): lone FOO label 1 IU (s1) and 2 IU (s2) beside the 1x stub path, with KiCad truth for the stub geometry; Pk = proposal_impl reloaded with my own integer TestSegmentHit(1) replacing the exact _on_segment. Plus v08_m_tolerance_and_glines.out t2 (connect_pins, foreign wire end 1 IU from pin 1) with a hand-built control of the route alone. L13, L10e and L09c not rebuilt; v06 Ke reproduces L10e's KiCad truth.

title: P as built misses a label 1 IU off the target's own wire or crossing, so it wires a pin KiCad already has on another named net
verifier_method: pr57pt/verify-probe-labels/v05_capture.py (.out) cases w1 (FOO 1 IU off own wire W1's interior), w2 (2 IU) and x1 (FOO 1 IU off both W1 and a foreign wire crossing it, L02d analog); KiCad truth before; P, Pk, M, B.

title: P's stated reason for refusing the label on the pin is wrong for one wire; the real trigger is a second line within 1 IU
verifier_method: pr57pt/verify-probe-labels/v06_label_on_pin.py (.out): KiCad-only label N on P with one foreign wire through P (Ka), plus the own wire ending at P (Kb), two crossing foreign wires (Kc), an off-grid wire 1 IU away plus own wire (Ke) or alone (Kf), and NEW a bus through P plus own wire (Kbus); tool level Ta (Ka geometry) and Tbus on P/M/B.

title: P keeps connect_pins' auto label, so naming that net later, or joining two connect_pins nets, is refused as a two-named-net merge
verifier_method: pr57pt/verify-probe-labels/v07_autolabel.py (.out): connect_pins(R1:1,R2:2) then wire_pins_to_net([R2:2],'N'), naming through the pin that does not carry the label; and connect_pins twice then connect_pins(R1:1,R3:1) on aligned pins; each design on its own file.
